entities.summary:
Paleolithic is a culture that emerged during the Classical era, spanning across the globe. It is characterized by the earliest human tools and art, created by early humans who migrated out of Africa around 60,000 years ago. This era is marked by the development of early languages and the emergence of early human societies, which were shaped by the harsh conditions of the Paleolithic environment.

    The core events of the Paleolithic era include the migration of early humans out of Africa, the development of early tools and technology, and the emergence of early human societies. The most notable achievements of this era include the creation of early art, music, and dance, as well as the development of early languages and writing systems.

    The legacy of the Paleolithic era can be seen in the modern-day cultures of Africa, Europe, and Asia, which continue to draw on the traditions and innovations of this era. The Paleolithic era also laid the groundwork for the development of modern science, technology, and society.

    The final statement of the Paleolithic era is the arrival of the Neolithic era, which marked the beginning of the agricultural revolution and the transition from a nomadic to a sedentary way of life.

    The impact of the Paleolithic era can be seen in the modern-day cultures of Africa, Europe, and Asia, which continue to draw on the traditions and innovations of this era.
